correctness.rationale: The stationary equations yield \(S'= -r\rho\) and \(R'=-(r+\alpha)\sigma\), a conserved quadratic flux and \(S=cR\) under positive outward current. Thus \(R'=-\Lambda\rho\); integrating this exact identity from the gas interface to infinity yields gas half-mass \(J/\Lambda\) for every admissible f. The dense R=u rho equation yields an exponential, and its integrated mass fixes b exactly. The injection jump \(S(0^+)=rM/2\), phase current continuity, positivity and all endpoints were reconstructed. Strict concavity makes the lower inverse unique and permits the fold expansion. Derivative of log(z)/z proves the unique optimal width. Distinct nonlinear gas-law profiles were verified with numerical quadrature and implicit differentiation but the general claim relies on proof, not finite computations.

originality.rationale: Compared actual claims: Grange proves the flux first integral for general velocities but solves the gas/liquid diagram for one specific linear dilute flux, then studies a prescribed finite-return rescaling. Its special-case width formula, thresholds, and any algebraic consequence for that one current are prior coverage. The evaluated result is instead the all-strictly-concave-current classification, simultaneous gas-only fold and universal droplet width, and the exact e-ratio topology for deformations of the current. Two explicit laws exhibit different all-gas existence at identical optimal droplet parameters. General MIPS reviews lack local-reset renewal source. Targeted mathematical-record searches returned unrelated matches. Residual priority risk is a more general prior flux-balance theorem or recognizing the extension as implicit in Grange Eq. (9).

value.rationale: A physically motivated exact model was previously solved for one linear gas motility law, leaving open which droplet features persist under nonlinear speed laws. The result shows that maximal droplet geometry and its \(1-1/e\) condensed fraction are invariant throughout a broad constitutive class, but gas-only coexistence is not: the sharp universal ratio \(F_{\max}/J=e\) separates two qualitatively distinct optimizers. The explicit linear-versus-quadratic gas flux example demonstrates model-design relevance independent of a numerical table or trivial parameter tweak.
